subject: chemistry
title: The Gases We Breathe
welcome_lead: Take a deep breath: a mix of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases fills your lungs.
meta_desc: Discover the composition of the atmosphere in this KS3 chemistry adventure on air.
final_note: You now know exactly what's in the air around you.

concepts.def: About 78% of the atmosphere; mostly unreactive.
About 21% of the atmosphere; needed for breathing and burning.
Around 0.9% of air; a noble gas.
About 0.04% of air but increasing slowly.
The mixture of gases held to Earth by gravity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Air is a mixture of gases. About 78% is nitrogen and 21% is oxygen. The remaining 1% is mostly argon, with traces of carbon dioxide, water vapour and other gases.

78% N₂, 21% O₂, 1% other.
You breathe in oxygen and breathe out more carbon dioxide. Fires need oxygen too — without it, a candle in a sealed jar quickly goes out.

Oxygen test: a glowing splint relights.
CO₂ test: turns limewater milky/cloudy.
Hydrogen test: a lit splint gives a squeaky pop.

options: Squeaky pop test
Limewater turns milky
Glowing splint relights

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.

mcqs.q: Why are most transition metal complex ions coloured?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels; electrons absorb visible light to jump between them (d-d transitions), and the complementary colour is transmitted.
Transition metal ions are coloured because they have a half-full d-subshell which naturally absorbs light.

mcqs.q: Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.
Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
